cleanIntro: Smith & Wesson prints two different SW1911 field strips — one for models with a barrel bushing, one for models without — and which one you follow is decided by the muzzle end of your pistol, not by preference. Deep Clean is the magazine, which the manual documents separately.

steps.title: Look at the muzzle: barrel bushing, or no barrel bushing?
steps.action: Before you touch a tool, look at the front of the slide. Some SW1911 models use a barrel bushing and a recoil spring retainer that turns with a wrench; other models have no barrel bushing and use a reverse spring retainer instead. This manual carries a separate disassembly procedure for each, and they are not interchangeable. Note the model number and serial number stamped on the frame at the same time; Smith & Wesson asks owners to record the serial number before shipping a pistol in for service, and quotes model number, dash number and serial number when ordering parts.
steps.prose: The bushing model has a visible ring around the barrel at the muzzle with a plug beside it; the bushingless models, typically the sub-compacts, have a bull barrel filling the slide opening and a captive spring assembly behind it. Applying the wrench procedure to a bushingless pistol accomplishes nothing, and trying to shortcut a bushing gun by skipping the wrench releases the recoil spring uncontrolled.
steps.quote: consult the appropriate section of this manual for specific instructions regarding the disassembly and assembly of your particular model of firearm
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Model and Features Identification, FIGURE 3c note, p.12
steps.warn: Steps 3 to 6 below are the BARREL BUSHING procedure. Steps 7 and 8 are the NO BARREL BUSHING procedure. Follow only the set that matches your pistol.

steps.title: Hammer back to safe, magazine out, chamber cleared
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction with your finger off the trigger. Ensure the hammer is fully rearward and put the safety lever fully up in the SAFE position, then press the magazine release and remove the magazine. Drop the safety to FIRE, draw the slide briskly fully rearward to extract anything in the chamber, and look into the chamber to confirm it is empty.
steps.prose: The order is particular to a 1911: the thumb safety only engages with the hammer cocked, so hammer first, safety second, and only then the magazine. Do not obstruct the ejection port while cycling the slide — a hand over it turns a chambered round into a jam instead of an ejection.
steps.quote: Ensure that the hammer is fully rearward and then place the safety lever in the fully up "safe" position (FIGURE 18).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Unloading, p.24

steps.title: BARREL BUSHING MODELS: wrench on, retainer depressed
steps.action: Grip the pistol firmly, put the wrench supplied with the pistol over the front of the slide and use it to depress the recoil spring retainer. Keep the retainer under the wrench the whole time.
steps.prose: That plug is sitting on a fully compressed recoil spring and it is the part that hurts people on a 1911. The wrench exists so your thumb is not what is holding it — if you have lost the factory wrench, do not improvise this step with a screwdriver blade, because the plug will jump the moment the bushing turns.
steps.quote: Firmly grasp the pistol as shown (FIGURE 22) and use the wrench provided and depress the recoil spring retainer.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With A Barrel Bushing, p.26
steps.warn: The recoil spring is under pressure. You must control the spring and plunger to prevent it from flying out and causing injury.

steps.title: BARREL BUSHING MODELS: bushing a quarter turn clockwise, retainer and spring out
steps.action: With the retainer still depressed, turn the wrench and barrel bushing clockwise about a quarter turn until the recoil spring retainer and recoil spring are free. Maintain your grip on the retainer as it pushes out, and catch the recoil spring.
steps.prose: Clockwise as you look at the muzzle, and only a quarter turn — the bushing's flange clears the retainer at that point and no further rotation is wanted yet. The spring will push the retainer out at you as soon as the bushing frees it; let it out slowly rather than letting the wrench slip off.
steps.quote: Turn the wrench and barrel bushing clockwise, approximately 1/4 turn until the recoil spring retainer and recoil spring are free to be removed.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With A Barrel Bushing, p.26

steps.title: BARREL BUSHING MODELS: slide stop out, slide off, guide rod out
steps.action: Fully cock the hammer to make the slide easier to push back, then move the slide rearward until the takedown notch in the slide lines up with the slide stop. Press inward on the slide stop pin from the right side of the frame and pull the slide stop out from the left, then run the slide forward off the frame. Turn the slide bottom up, rotate the barrel link up for clearance, and lift the recoil spring guide rod up and back out.
steps.prose: Cocking the hammer takes the mainspring load off the slide and is what makes this a two-finger job instead of a fight. The notch has to be aligned before the slide stop will come out — pulling on a misaligned stop gouges a crescent into the frame above the trigger, which is the classic 1911 idiot mark. The barrel link must be rotated up or the guide rod has nowhere to go.
steps.quote: Press inward on the slide stop pin from the right side of the frame and remove the slide stop from the left side (FIGURE 25).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With A Barrel Bushing, p.26

steps.title: BARREL BUSHING MODELS: bushing out the front, then the barrel
steps.action: Rotate the barrel bushing counterclockwise until its lug lines up with the opening between the barrel hole and the recoil spring hole, and pull the bushing out the front of the slide. Then rotate the barrel link forward into its lowered position and draw the barrel out through the front of the slide.
steps.prose: The bushing only leaves through that one angular position, so if it will not come out it has not been rotated far enough round. The barrel goes out the front, not the back, and the link has to be lowered first — a link left standing up catches on the slide's lower lug recess and stops the barrel dead.
steps.quote: Rotate the barrel link to the forward position (lowered) and remove the barrel through the front of the slide (FIGURE 29).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With A Barrel Bushing, p.27

steps.title: NO BARREL BUSHING MODELS: slide stop out, slide off with the spring contained
steps.action: On a bushingless SW1911 there is no wrench step at all. Cock the hammer, move the slide back until the takedown notch aligns with the slide stop, press the slide stop pin inward from the right and remove the stop entirely from the left. Then move the slide forward off the frame while keeping your hand around the recoil spring assembly, turn the slide bottom up, lift the back end of the guide rod and release the spring tension slowly before removing guide rod and spring from under the barrel.
steps.prose: The whole spring load comes off in this one movement rather than being staged by a wrench, which is why the manual tells you to keep a hand around the assembly as the slide leaves the frame. Release the tension by lifting the rear of the guide rod slowly — letting go at this point sends the rod and spring across the room.
steps.quote: Move the slide forward and remove it from the frame, while keeping your hand around the recoil spring assembly to prevent it from flying out (FIGURE 36).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With No Barrel Bushing, p.29

steps.title: NO BARREL BUSHING MODELS: retainer plug out, then the barrel
steps.action: Remove the recoil spring retainer plug from the front of the slide, then draw the barrel out through the front of the slide.
steps.prose: With no bushing there is nothing gripping the barrel at the muzzle, so once the plug is out the barrel simply slides forward. It still goes out the front — a bushingless bull barrel will not come out the back of the slide, and levering at it from the breech end only marks the hood.
steps.quote: Remove the recoil spring retainer plug as shown (FIGURES 38 and 39).
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping / Disassembly For Models With No Barrel Bushing, p.30

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Frame, slide, barrel, barrel link, recoil spring, guide rod, magazine, and — on a bushing model — the bushing and recoil spring retainer. That is as far as Smith & Wesson takes an SW1911. Do not dry fire the pistol with the slide off. When parts go back on, use only genuine SW1911 parts: parts from other brands of pistols must never be used in your SW1911 even though they may appear similar.
steps.prose: The parts warning matters most on this platform because the 1911 pattern has the largest aftermarket of any pistol design, and a bushing, plug, link or slide stop from another maker will very often fit and still be wrong. Deep Clean covers the magazine, which the manual documents on its own.
steps.quote: PARTS FROM OTHER BRANDS OF PISTOLS MUST NEVER BE USED IN YOUR SW1911 EVEN THOUGH THE PARTS MAY APPEAR TO BE SIMILAR. USE OF ANY PARTS OTHER THAN GENUINE SW1911 PARTS MAY CAUSE A SERIOUS MALFUNCTION RESULTING IN INJURY OR DEATH TO YOU OR OTHERS AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Field Stripping Disassembly, WARNING, p.27 (repeated p.29)

deepSteps.title: Clear the magazine and the bench
deepSteps.action: Remove all cartridges from the magazine and from your work area before you start.
deepSteps.prose: The manual asks for the work area to be clear as well as the magazine, and that is not fussiness — a magazine strip puts a spring and a small catch into the air, and loose rounds on the bench are exactly what a dropped part disappears among. It also removes any chance of a live round finding its way back into a magazine you are about to reassemble.
deepSteps.quote: Remove all cartridges from the magazine and your work area.
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.36
deepSteps.warn: The magazine spring is under pressure. Control the spring and follower so that they do not fly out and cause injury.

deepSteps.title: Depress the buttplate catch through the buttplate hole
deepSteps.action: Use a drift punch through the hole in the magazine buttplate to depress the buttplate catch inside the tube.
deepSteps.prose: The catch is a small tab held up against the buttplate by the magazine spring, and the hole is only just big enough for a punch of the right size. Something too large will not reach the catch at all, and something sharp that slips will burr the inside of the tube where the follower has to run.
deepSteps.quote: Using a drift punch, depress the buttplate catch (4) through hole in the magazine buttplate. (5)
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.36

deepSteps.title: Buttplate off, catch and spring out
deepSteps.action: Slide the magazine buttplate off the tube while holding the buttplate catch down inside it, then take the catch and the spring out through the bottom of the tube.
deepSteps.prose: Keep pressure on that catch until the buttplate is fully clear — the moment the plate stops covering it, the spring is pushing catch and spring out of the bottom. A 1911 magazine spring is long and holds enough energy to send the catch a good distance.
deepSteps.quote: Slide magazine buttplate (5) off of the magazine tube (1) while holding the buttplate catch (4) in the magazine tube (1).
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.36

deepSteps.title: Follower out of the bottom, then clean the tube
deepSteps.action: Turn the magazine tube right side up and remove the follower through the bottom of the tube. Clean the inside of the tube, the follower and the spring while they are apart.
deepSteps.prose: Note which way round the follower sits before it leaves: it goes back with its stepped edge toward the round side of the tube, and a follower installed the other way round will nose-dive .45 ACP rounds into the feed ramp. Residue inside the tube is the usual reason a magazine that used to hold seven rounds now sticks on the last two.
deepSteps.quote: Turn magazine tube (1) right side up and remove magazine follower (3) through the bottom of the magazine tube (1).
deepSteps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
SW1911 Pistols & 
SW1911 E-Series
™Pistols — REV:SW1911_080118 — Magazine Disassembly, p.36

cleaning.name: BARREL AND CHAMBER
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and chamber with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish with a dry cotton cloth patch through the bore to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the feed ramp, the barrel hood and the locking lugs on top of the barrel
Clean the barrel link and its pin area, and check the link swings freely

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BUSHING AND FRAME
tasks: Clean the breech face, extractor and firing pin channel opening
Clean the inside of the slide including the locking lug recesses
On bushing models, clean the bushing inside and out and the recoil spring retainer
Clean the frame rails, the slide stop crosspin hole and the magazine well
Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth and remove all solution, oil and fingerprints

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe the tube and the feed lips
If the magazine has been apart, clean the inside of the tube, the follower and the spring before reassembly
Check the buttplate is locked on before the magazine goes back into service

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: Four lubrication points on the slide, plus the top of the barrel and the top of the recoil spring guide rod — one drop of firearm lubricant each
Do not over-lubricate: excess collects unburned powder and carbon residue and interferes with proper functioning
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning
Never use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on this pistol

reassembly: Assemble in the reverse of the procedure you used, and use only genuine SW1911 parts.

BARREL BUSHING MODELS: barrel in through the front of the slide with the link lowered, then the bushing in and rotated clockwise into place, then the guide rod, then the slide onto the frame and the slide stop in from the left with the takedown notch aligned. Fit the recoil spring and retainer last, using the wrench to depress the retainer while turning the bushing counterclockwise a quarter turn to capture it.

NO BARREL BUSHING MODELS: barrel in through the front of the slide, guide rod and recoil spring under the barrel, retainer plug in, then the slide onto the frame and the slide stop in from the left with the notch aligned.

MAGAZINE: install the follower with its stepped edge toward the round side of the tube, then the spring and buttplate catch, then slide the buttplate on until the circular projection of the catch engages it.
E-Series pistols reassemble exactly as the standard SW1911 does, except that they use a titanium firing pin and have no firing pin plunger or plunger lever to catch on the slide as it goes back.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, hand-cycle the slide several times and confirm it runs fully into battery and that the slide stop locks it open on an empty magazine and releases cleanly. On a bushing model check the bushing is rotated fully home and the recoil spring retainer is captured — a partly turned bushing lets the plug launch on the first shot. Check the thumb safety engages only with the hammer cocked and locks the slide and trigger, and that the grip safety releases the trigger when the grip is taken properly. Then seat an empty magazine and confirm it latches and drops free.
